runtime_ui_status: PARTIAL_PRIOR_EVIDENCE — actor/API response, peer detail/list/actions passed; related stock-level API refetch changed per-location values but the table cell was not separately asserted; dashboards and other transitions unverified.
evidence_or_reason: The stock transfer writes inventory movement/stock levels in the same transaction before the order status update. StockMovementCompleted and TransferOrderChanged use their existing post-commit refresh paths; the central transfer_order map covers stock/location/dashboard queries. Delta 578: Delta 578: two-context headless Chromium run (System Administrator actor, Warehouse Staff peer) executed this transfer with the actor socket closed. The peer received one private record event and one entity-list event, refetched both authorized detail/list endpoints, rendered Transferred, and removed Execute/Cancel without reload; actor rendered the API response immediately. Peer detail/list UI completion was 1,493 ms after actor HTTP response, one sample (not commit-to-UI p95). Related stock/map/dashboard, badges, inbox and other transitions remain unverified. The first failed-after-execute attempt and passing rerun each moved one whole unit in dev; both authorized DB movements remain. Delta 579 stock follow-up: a second Warehouse tab subscribed to private inventory.dashboard, received one InventoryStockChanged event and issued a successful stock-level GET; a separate authorized read confirmed per-location quantities changed. Latest detail/list/stock response offsets were 1,134/1,705/2,530 ms from the timestamp after actor response-body read; stock table-cell render was not separately asserted and this one stock sample exceeded 2 seconds. Event offsets were −116/−116/−123 ms relative to that timestamp and are not commit-to-event latency. transition_definition: PurchaseRequestService::approve() locks and requires Pending; only the final completed approval step calls markApproved()
evidence_or_reason: Delta 631: one real-backend role-separated Chromium run advanced a synthetic PR from the VP approval step to Approved. The actor socket was blocked; the API response updated the VP actor; the open System Administrator detail rendered Approved and removed Cancel after an authorized GET at 1,650 ms; the Purchasing creator list rendered Approved at 2,142 ms. The detail response carried actions.can_cancel=false and was not served by a service worker; cache headers were no-store/private with CF-Cache-Status DYNAMIC. Three private chain refresh frames were received. Network instrumentation recorded one overlapping detail GET started +67 ms and canceled +201 ms, followed by one successful authorized GET started +197 ms and completed at +1,614 ms; the cancellation is central invalidation behavior to supersede an in-flight read after a record signal. The log closed at the successful render and does not rule out a later queued catch-up. A separate earlier run had inconsistent timing; p95 and badges/dashboards/linked-record/inbox outcomes remain unverified. Delta 972 isolated four-context scenario: VP PATCH returned approved with actor socket disabled; peer received three private refresh frames, then a no-store authorized GET returned approved/actions.can_cancel=false. The peer status/action render was +4.270 s and creator list +4.616 s from actor response; the test failed its 2 s detail assertion. Queue telemetry recorded 2.300–3.294 s waits for chain broadcasts while 60 outbox dispatch jobs and 22 dashboard-widget events were processed on one E2E worker consuming high before broadcasts. Dev runtime uses distinct Horizon supervisors; this test-stack mismatch does not establish equivalent dev queue delay. The E2E queue split was corrected, but its only rerun timed out on the create page before writing a record, so no after-change latency result is claimed.
